newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia media laws limit investment - report.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia media laws limit investment - report.

text.p: Australia's media and telecommunications laws are preventing new and diverse operators from investing in the industry, according to a report released on Monday.

The Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT) Media and Telecommunications Group report said this was happening as a result of the multiple layers of regulation and opportunities for political interference.
In addition, the rapid changes in technology and new media were outpacing law-making, the report said.
"Freedom of communication is endangered whenever politicians or bureau have power, as they do at present, to decide who should own the media," group director Mark Armstrong said.
"Better laws would give more encouragement for investment in media and freedom of speech," he said.
"Free speech requires prosperous, stable Australian media without political control or monopolisation," he said.
Armstrong said the regulatory system needed to be replaced with rules which were legislated, in black and white, by parliament. "The current laws are ageing rapidly," he said.
"Australian media is likely to flourish if old and new media know in advance what the rules of the game will be," he said.
The RMIT report was published following a round-table seminar involving senior media and telecommunications industry executives and policy experts.
The Australian government is currently considering a review of the media industry, which could lead to changes to ownership rules and regulation.
The telecommunications industry will be de-regulated in July next year in order to allow new players to enter the market.
